title: Google rolls back AI Google Earth feature a day after launch
excerpt: Google added Nano Banana 2 image generation into Google Earth. Misinformation attempts ensued.
content_html:
After Google added its AI image generator, Nano Banana, to Google Earth on Thursday, it reversed its decision a day later.

Google announced the addition of Nano Banana 2 into its mapping platform, presumably to help users generate infographics about a site, see what it looked like historically, generate real estate ideas, and other use cases. Instead, as 404 Media observed, it made it very easy to inject misinformation into Google Earth, including making it appear like a nuclear strike had hit a location or that protests had taken over Google's offices.

On Thursday, Google seemed to try to smooth out the kinks, sharing on Thursday night on X that "every image created with Nano Banana in Google Earth includes the SynthID digital watermark, so if someone is unsure about an image, they can ask the Gemini app or use Lens in Search to see if the image was AI-generated." It also stated that it prevents image creation on "harmful topics."

However, come Friday afternoon, Google announced on X that it was removing the feature:

We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world. We've seen geospatial professionals using this feature for a range of useful purposes, however we've also seen people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies. So we're rolling back this feature in Google Earth while we work on implementing stronger guardrails. It's important to note that generated images didn’t appear in the main Google Earth experience for others to see and were watermarked as AI generated.

The backlash to the initial decision was quick. Replies to the rollback post on X include Gravity Falls creator Alex Hirsch saying, "You guys are living in a complete bubble. Step outside Silicon Valley for two seconds and you'll realize no actual human wants AI sludge crammed into every corner of every product. Touch grass. Talk to actual people."

Another top reply read, "There is 0 chance that no one on your development team didn't raise exactly this concern."

content_html_zh:
周四，谷歌将其人工智能图像生成器 Nano Banana 添加到 Google Earth 后，一天后又改变了决定。

谷歌宣布将 Nano Banana 2 添加到其地图平台中，大概是为了帮助用户生成有关某个站点的信息图表、了解它的历史情况、生成房地产创意和其他用例。 相反，正如 404 Media 所观察到的那样，它使得向 Google 地球注入错​​误信息变得非常容易，包括使其看起来像是核袭击袭击了某个地点，或者抗议活动占领了 Google 办公室。

周四，谷歌似乎试图消除这些问题，周四晚上在 X 上分享称，“在 Google Earth 中使用 Nano Banana 创建的每张图像都包含 SynthID 数字水印，因此如果有人不确定图像，他们可以询问 Gemini 应用程序或使用 Lens in Search 来查看图像是否是 AI 生成的。” 它还表示，它可以防止创建有关“有害主题”的图像。

然而，周五下午，谷歌在 X 上宣布将删除该功能：

我们知道，人们特别相信 Google 地球能够提供可靠的世界观。 我们已经看到地理空间专业人士将此功能用于一系列有用的目的，但我们也看到人们分享了似乎违反我们政策的生成图像的屏幕截图。 因此，我们将在 Google 地球中回滚此功能，同时努力实施更强大的护栏。 值得注意的是，生成的图像不会出现在主要的 Google 地球体验中供其他人查看，并且在人工智能生成时带有水印。

最初的决定很快遭到了强烈反对。 《重力瀑布》的创作者亚历克斯·赫希 (Alex Hirsch) 在 X 上回复了回滚帖子，他说：“你们生活在一个完全的泡沫中。 走出硅谷两秒钟，你就会意识到没有人愿意将人工智能污泥塞进每个产品的每个角落。 触摸草。 与真实的人交谈。”

另一条热门回复写道：“您的开发团队中没有人没有提出这一问题的可能性为零。”
